subject: Planned maintenance: EU-North rolling node driver update (Dec 15-16)
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Date: Sat, 12 Dec 2026 08:30:00 +0000
Subject: Planned maintenance: EU-North rolling node driver update (Dec 15-16)

Hi Rachel / team,

Heads up — Redwood will perform a staged GPU driver and micro-kernel rollout across our eu-north (eun-1) inferencing fleet. This is a planned maintenance window to address an intermittent kernel hang observed in specific GPU/driver combinations (see attached changelog).

High-level plan
- Window: Tue Dec 15 22:00 UTC — Wed Dec 16 04:00 UTC (we will keep the work to this window but can shift if you have constraints)
- Scope: rolling restarts of inference nodes in eun-1 (subset by rack to avoid bulk impact)
- Per-node impact: service process restart and driver swap, expected 2-6 minutes of transient connection loss per node
- Customer-visible impact: No full-region outage expected. Typical effect is a handful of requests re-routed to healthy nodes; we expect request-level retries to succeed. If you have long-lived pinned connections, you may see transient errors.

Attachments: maintenance-matrix.csv (node order + time estimates), driver-changelog-1.2.3.pdf
Links: JIRA INF-2048 and rollout plan in the shared Drive (link below)

Mitigations we will apply
- Canary run in a single fault domain ahead of the window
- Staggered inter-rack delays to keep sufficient capacity online
- Automatic fallback to compatible driver build on node failure
- 24/7 on-call coverage from Redwood infra during the window (contact details below)

Questions for you
1) Do you have any blackout sub-windows (e.g., scheduled jobs, data exports) between the proposed window?
2) Any dedicated or pinned capacity in eun-1 we should avoid touching? If yes, please send the cluster/node IDs.

If you’re OK with the dates above we’ll schedule a canary at Tue Dec 15 21:00 UTC (one rack) and proceed to staged rollout at 22:00 UTC.

Status page: https://status.redwood.com/incidents/INF-2048
JIRA: INF-2048
Drive: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/0ABC123eun-maintenance

Thanks,
Marissa Cole

1) We run a mix of Hosted API and a single Private VPC deployment in eun-1. Will the Private VPC endpoints be touched by this driver swap? We have long-running streaming sessions for a handful of inference jobs and want to avoid interruptions.

Hi Rachel / Marissa — quick technical follow-up from infra: 

Short answers first:
- Private VPC: If you are using Redwood Private (customer-managed control plane + nodes in your VPC), we will not touch customer-managed nodes unless you have previously opted into Redwood-managed driver upgrades. Based on our records, AcmeCloud's Private deployment is configured for "Redwood-managed infra" — but we will exclude any nodes explicitly flagged as "do-not-update". Please send node IDs if you want exclusions.
- Reserved/Dedicated capacity: Reserved pools are included only when customers opt into minor driver maintenance; by default we avoid touching isolated reserved nodes during routine rollouts. For RSRV-ACME-2025 we see no opt-in flag, so we will schedule reserved capacity at the end of the window if you request.
- SLA/rollback: There is an expedited rollback plan in the attachments (driver-changelog-1.2.3.pdf) — if the canary shows regressions we will halt and roll back within 30–45 minutes. SLA credit requests follow the standard enterprise SLA process; we'll engage CS/Finance immediately on any material downtime.

Operational details:
- Canary: proposed Tue Dec 15 21:00 UTC (single fault domain) — 10–15 minute observation period.
- Rollout cadence: 1 rack every ~12 minutes (configurable); per-node disruption 2–4 minutes expected for process restart; driver install can extend to 6 minutes for older kernels.
- Monitoring: we'll watch latency percentiles and error rates; we’ll post updates to the status page and the JIRA ticket.

Next steps for us (if Acme confirms):
1) Schedule canary Tue 15 21:00 UTC
2) Exclude any nodes Acme flags as do-not-update
3) If canary passes, proceed staged rollout starting 22:00 UTC

Attaching canary plan: eun-rollout-canary-plan.md

--

Principal Infra Engineer, Redwood Inference
